caption: A plain integer has length zero

wolfram.note: compute-engine folds Sqrt(7) into an exact numeric-literal value (operator 'Real', no operands) rather than keeping it structurally as Power(7, 1/2); Length reads operand count, which is legitimately 0 for a numeric literal here even though Wolfram's FullForm keeps Power[7,1/2] as a 2-operand expression. Same representational root cause as NumberQ's Sqrt(2)/Infinity rows
sage.note: Ours folds Sqrt(7) into a numeric literal, an atom of length 0; Wolfram and Sage keep Power(7, 1/2) with two operands. Ours is the odd one out.
sympy.note: SymPy keeps sqrt(7) as Pow(7, 1/2), two arguments; compute-engine folds it into a numeric literal, an atom.
